initial_question: What kind of headache are you suffering from?

options.label: Sudden Excruciating 'Thunderclap' or Stiff Neck with Fever
options.description: Sudden severe pain reaching maximum intensity within seconds, or headache with neck stiffness, fever, or confusion.
options.subtype_name: Thunderclap Headache / Suspected Meningitis or Brain Bleed
options.warning: 🚨 CRITICAL EMERGENCY: A sudden 'thunderclap' headache or headache with stiff neck/fever requires IMMEDIATE emergency medical care.
first_aid_steps: Call 112 (or local emergency medical services) immediately.
Keep the person lying down in a quiet, dark, and calm environment.
Do not give any pain medication, food, or drinks until evaluated by paramedics.
Monitor responsiveness, alertness, and breathing closely.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate emergency room / 112 dispatch required.

options.label: Throbbing Pain on One Side with Light/Sound Sensitivity or Nausea
options.description: Pulsating or throbbing pain usually on one side of the head, often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, or visual disturbances (aura).
options.warning: Migraines can be debilitating. Rest in a dark, quiet environment. (Note: Women are 3x more likely to experience hormonal migraines).
first_aid_steps: Rest in a quiet, dark, well-ventilated room with eyes closed.
Apply a cool damp cloth or cold compress across your forehead or back of neck.
Sip water slowly to stay hydrated.
If prescribed, take migraine relief medication early during the attack.
Avoid bright screens, loud noises, and strong odors.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a doctor if migraines recur frequently, increase in severity, or fail to respond to standard medications.

options.label: Dull Aching Pressure Like a Tight Band Around Forehead or Neck
options.description: Constant dull ache felt on both sides of head, forehead, or back of neck, often caused by stress, posture, or fatigue.
options.warning: Tension headaches are common and usually resolve with rest, relaxation, and hydration.
first_aid_steps: Apply a warm compress or heating pad to neck and shoulder muscles to ease muscle tension.
Perform gentle neck stretches and shoulder rolls.
Drink plenty of fresh water to ensure hydration.
Over-the-counter pain relievers (like paracetamol or ibuprofen) may help if tolerated.
Take a short break from computer screens and practice relaxed deep breathing.
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a primary physician if tension headaches occur more than 2-3 times a week.

options.label: Severe Sharp Piercing Pain Around One Eye with Eye Watering
options.description: Intense burning or piercing pain around one eye or temple, accompanied by eye redness, tearing, or drooping eyelid.
options.warning: Cluster headaches produce intense localized pain. Professional medical evaluation is recommended.
first_aid_steps: Sit upright in a comfortable chair—avoid lying down as it can worsen cluster pain.
Breathe deeply in fresh, cool air.
Apply a cool towel over the affected eye and temple.
Contact your doctor for high-flow oxygen therapy or specialized prescription treatments.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Requires evaluation by a neurologist or physician for targeted cluster headache preventive therapy.

options.label: Deep Facial Pressure Behind Cheeks, Forehead, & Nasal Congestion
options.description: Deep, constant pain around cheekbones, forehead, or bridge of nose, worsening when bending forward, accompanied by nasal discharge.
options.warning: Sinus headaches are associated with sinus congestion or infection.
first_aid_steps: Inhale warm steam from a bowl of hot water or shower to open nasal passages.
Apply warm moist compresses around nose, cheeks, and eyes.
Use saline nasal spray to clear congestion.
Stay hydrated with warm fluids like tea or clear broth.
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if sinus pain lasts over 10 days or is accompanied by high fever and purulent nasal discharge.

initial_question: What type of chest pain or chest discomfort are you having?

options.label: Heavy Squeezing Pressure Spreading to Arm/Jaw with Sweating & Breathlessness
options.description: Crushing pressure or pain in center of chest, radiating to left arm, neck, jaw, or back, with shortness of breath or cold sweat.
options.warning: 🚨 LIFE-THREATENING EMERGENCY: Suspected heart attack requires immediate emergency medical dispatch. (Note for Women: Female heart attack symptoms often present as severe fatigue, shortness of breath, nausea, or jaw/back pain without sharp chest pain).
first_aid_steps: Call 112 (or emergency services) immediately.
Help the person sit down in a comfortable position (leaning back with knees bent) to relieve strain on the heart.
Loosen tight clothing around neck and chest.
If conscious and not allergic, administer 300mg aspirin to chew slowly (if recommended by emergency dispatcher).
Be prepared to perform CPR if the person loses consciousness and stops normal breathing.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate 112 ambulance response required.

options.label: Sharp Pain That Gets Worse When Breathing Deeply or Coughing
options.description: Sharp knife-like pain in side of chest aggravated by deep inhalation, coughing, or laughing.
options.subtype_name: Pleuritic Chest Pain / Possible Pulmonary Issue
options.warning: Pleuritic chest pain requires medical investigation to check for pneumonia, pleurisy, or pulmonary embolism.
first_aid_steps: Sit in a comfortable upright position.
Take shallow, gentle breaths rather than deep forced inhalations.
Rest calmly and avoid physical strain.
Seek urgent medical evaluation at a hospital or urgent care clinic.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Seek medical evaluation immediately, especially if accompanied by fever, cough, or leg swelling.

options.label: Burning Sensation Behind Breastbone After Eating / Worse When Lying Down
options.description: Burning pain rising into throat, often after heavy or spicy meals, improving with antacids.
options.warning: Heartburn is common but can mimic chest discomfort. Ensure non-cardiac origin.
first_aid_steps: Sit upright—do not lie down flat immediately after eating.
Sip water or chew non-mint gum to help neutralize stomach acid.
Take over-the-counter antacid medication if appropriate.
Loosen tight belts or waistbands.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a doctor if heartburn occurs frequently or swallowing becomes painful.

options.label: Aching Pain That Gets Worse When Pressing on Chest Wall or Moving Torso
options.description: Localized tenderness when pushing on ribs or sternum, often triggered by heavy lifting or physical strain.
options.warning: Muscle strain in chest is non-cardiac but should be evaluated if pain changes.
first_aid_steps: Rest and avoid heavy lifting or torso twisting.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in a cloth to tender chest area for 15 minutes.
Take mild over-the-counter pain relievers if tolerated.
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if chest pain is persistent or fails to improve within a few days.

initial_question: Where and what type of stomach/abdominal pain are you experiencing?

options.label: Sharp Pain Starting Near Navel and Moving to Lower Right Side
options.description: Severe localized pain in lower right quadrant of abdomen, getting worse with walking or coughing, with low fever and loss of appetite.
options.warning: 🚨 URGENT MEDICAL EMERGENCY: Suspected appendicitis requires prompt surgical evaluation.
first_aid_steps: Go to the emergency department or call 112 immediately.
Do NOT give anything to eat or drink (NPO status required for potential surgery).
Do NOT apply heat pads or give laxatives, as this could cause appendix rupture.
Keep the person resting quietly in a comfortable posture with knees drawn up.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate emergency department evaluation required.

options.label: Severe Lower Pelvic / Cramping Pain (Female Health Alert)
options.description: Sharp or cramping pain in lower pelvic region, potentially related to ectopic pregnancy, ovarian cyst, or severe menstrual dysmenorrhea.
options.subtype_name: Acute Pelvic Pain / Gynecological Medical Alert
options.warning: 🚨 FEMALE HEALTH ALERT: Sudden severe lower pelvic pain with dizziness or heavy vaginal bleeding can indicate an ectopic pregnancy rupture or ovarian torsion.
first_aid_steps: If accompanied by dizziness, faintness, or missed period, call 112 or visit Emergency Department immediately.
Rest flat with legs slightly elevated.
Apply a gentle warm hot-water bottle to lower abdomen if non-acute menstrual cramping is suspected.
Do not ingest heavy food until evaluated by a doctor.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate ER or Gynecologist evaluation required for acute severe pelvic pain.

options.label: Sudden Severe Groin or Testicular Pain Radiating to Lower Abdomen (Male Health Alert)
options.description: Sudden agonizing pain in scrotum, groin, or lower abdomen, with swelling or nausea.
options.subtype_name: Acute Groin / Suspected Testicular Torsion or Inguinal Hernia
options.warning: 🚨 MALE MEDICAL EMERGENCY: Testicular torsion requires emergency surgery within 6 hours to prevent tissue damage.
first_aid_steps: Go to the nearest Hospital Emergency Room immediately or call 112.
Do not delay seeking emergency medical attention.
Keep the person lying down and supported with ice pack over underwear if tolerated.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate ER surgical evaluation required within hours.

options.label: Burning Pain in Upper Stomach with Indigestion or Nausea
options.description: Gnawing or burning ache in upper abdomen, feeling worse or better after eating food.
options.warning: Upper stomach burning is often linked to gastric inflammation or stomach acid irritation.
first_aid_steps: Eat small, bland meals (toast, rice, applesauce) and avoid spicy, acidic, or fatty foods.
Avoid alcohol, caffeine, and NSAID pain relievers (like aspirin/ibuprofen).
Sip clear fluids slowly to stay hydrated.
Consider over-the-counter antacids.
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a physician if stomach pain persists over 1 week or if stool appears dark/tarry.

options.label: Wave-like Cramping Across Abdomen with Diarrhea or Gas
options.description: Diffused abdominal cramping with bloating, gurgling, or watery stools, usually due to stomach flu or food issues.
options.warning: Focus on rehydration and resting the digestive tract.
first_aid_steps: Sip oral rehydration solutions (ORS), clear broths, or electrolyte drinks to replace lost fluids.
Rest quietly with a warm water bottle placed gently on the stomach.
Follow the BRAT diet (Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast) when ready to eat.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a doctor if high fever, severe dehydration, or persistent bloody diarrhea occurs.

options.label: Unbearable Radiating Pain from Side to Lower Back / Groin
options.description: Sudden intense flank pain coming in waves, radiating from back to lower abdomen/groin, often with blood in urine.
options.warning: Renal colic pain is extremely intense and requires prompt medical diagnosis and pain management.
first_aid_steps: Seek urgent care or emergency room evaluation for diagnostic imaging and pain relief.
Drink plenty of water if able to swallow and not vomiting severely.
Apply warm compress to the lower back side area.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Seek emergency medical evaluation for unbearable flank pain or inability to pass urine.

options.label: High Fever (>103°F/39.4°C) with Stiff Neck, Rash, or Confusion
options.description: High temperature accompanied by inability to bend chin to chest, confusion, extreme drowsiness, or non-fading purple skin spots.
options.subtype_name: High Risk Fever / Suspected Severe Infection or Meningitis
options.warning: 🚨 CRITICAL WARNING: Fever combined with neck stiffness, confusion, or purple rash is a medical emergency.
first_aid_steps: Call 112 or transport immediately to nearest emergency medical center.
Keep the person calm, lying flat, and uncrowded.
Apply lukewarm (not cold) damp cloths to forehead and neck.
Do not submerge in ice baths.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate 112 emergency care.

options.label: Fever with Cough, Sore Throat, Body Aches, & Fatigue
options.description: Moderate to high temperature with common viral/flu symptoms like runny nose, body chills, and dry cough.
options.warning: Rest and continuous fluids are essential for recovery.
first_aid_steps: Get plenty of bed rest.
Drink abundant fluids (water, warm herbal tea, clear soups) to prevent dehydration.
Take over-the-counter fever reducers (acetaminophen/paracetamol or ibuprofen) as directed.
Dress in lightweight clothing and use thin blankets.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Seek medical advice if fever lasts more than 3 days or causes shortness of breath.

options.label: Mild Low-Grade Fever (<101°F/38.3°C) with Slight Shivering
options.description: Slight body temperature elevation with mild fatigue, resolving with basic rest.
options.warning: Monitor body temperature every few hours.
first_aid_steps: Rest comfortably in a moderately cooled room.
Sip room-temperature water continuously.
Monitor body temperature using a digital thermometer.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a doctor if fever rises above 102°F (38.9°C) or lasts over 72 hours.

initial_question: What best describes your breathing difficulty?

options.label: Severe Gasping for Air, Inability to Speak Full Words, or Blue Lips
options.description: Acute severe respiratory distress, struggles to speak a few words, bluish tint on lips/fingernails, or feeling suffocation.
options.warning: 🚨 CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Severe difficulty breathing requires immediate emergency paramedic assistance.
first_aid_steps: Call 112 immediately.
Sit the person upright in a comfortable position—leaning forward resting arms on a table can help ease breathing.
Loosen collars, neckties, belts, and tight clothing around waist/chest.
Keep surrounding area quiet and clear of crowding people.
Be prepared to perform CPR compressions if breathing stops.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate 112 emergency response.

options.label: High-Pitched Wheezing Sound with Chest Tightness
options.description: Whistling sound when breathing out, tight feeling in chest, often associated with asthma or allergic trigger.
options.warning: Use rescue inhaler immediately if available.
first_aid_steps: Sit upright calmly—do not lie down.
Help the person use their quick-relief rescue inhaler (Albuterol) with spacer (1 puff every 30-60 seconds, up to 4 puffs).
Encourage slow, deep breathing through the nose and out through pursed lips.
If no improvement after inhaler use, call emergency services immediately.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Seek emergency care if rescue inhaler does not relieve breathing difficulty within 5-10 minutes.

options.label: Mild Breathlessness After Exertion or with Stuffy Nose
options.description: Feeling slightly out of breath after walking up stairs or with nasal congestion during a cold.
options.warning: Rest until normal breathing rhythm is restored.
first_aid_steps: Stop physical activity and sit in a comfortable upright position.
Practice steady pursed-lip breathing.
Ventilate the room with fresh air.
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a physician if breathlessness occurs with minimal effort or during sleep.

initial_question: Which type of dizziness are you experiencing?

options.label: Dizziness with Sudden Face Drooping, Arm Weakness, or Slurred Speech (F.A.S.T.)
options.description: Sudden onset of dizziness combined with weakness on one side of body, facial asymmetry, or difficulty speaking.
options.warning: 🚨 CRITICAL EMERGENCY: F.A.S.T. stroke warning signs require immediate emergency hospital care.
first_aid_steps: Call 112 immediately and inform dispatcher of suspected stroke.
Note the exact time symptoms first started.
Lay the person down safely with head slightly elevated.
Do not give any food, water, or medication.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate 112 emergency call.

options.label: Sensation That the Room is Spinning Round and Round
options.description: False sense of movement or environment spinning, often aggravated by moving head position, with nausea.
options.warning: Avoid sudden head movements to prevent falls.
first_aid_steps: Sit or lie down immediately on a stable surface.
Keep your head still and focus on a fixed stationary object.
Avoid bright lights, sudden posture changes, and reading.
Avoid driving or operating machinery while experiencing vertigo.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Consult an ENT or doctor for vestibular evaluation if spinning recurs.

options.label: Feeling Faint or Woozy Upon Standing Up Rapidly
options.description: Brief wooziness or dark vision when standing up quickly, usually caused by temporary blood pressure dip or mild dehydration.
options.warning: Sit back down if feeling faint.
first_aid_steps: Sit down or lie flat with legs slightly elevated.
Sip 1-2 glasses of cool water to replenish fluids.
Stand up gradually in stages (sit on edge of bed first before standing).
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if lightheadedness leads to frequent fainting episodes.

initial_question: What kind of skin rash or skin reaction do you have?

options.label: Spreading Hives with Facial Swelling, Throat Tightness, or Gasping
options.description: Rapidly spreading red itchy welts accompanied by swelling of lips, tongue, or difficulty breathing.
options.warning: 🚨 CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Anaphylaxis is life-threatening. Use EpiPen immediately if available.
first_aid_steps: Call 112 immediately.
Administer Epinephrine Auto-Injector (EpiPen) into outer thigh if person has one.
Lay person flat on back (or sit slightly up if breathing is hard).
Stay with person and monitor breathing until help arrives.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate emergency room / 112 dispatch.

options.label: Red Raised Itchy Welts (Hives) Without Breathing Problems
options.description: Sudden itchy red bumps or hives across skin caused by food, insect sting, or mild allergy, without facial swelling.
options.warning: Monitor closely for any signs of breathing difficulty or lip swelling.
first_aid_steps: Apply cool damp compresses to soothe itchy skin.
Take an over-the-counter oral antihistamine (like cetirizine or diphenhydramine) if safe.
Avoid hot showers and scratchy clothing.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Seek emergency care immediately if facial swelling or breathing trouble develops.

options.label: Localized Red Itchy Rash After Touching Plant, Soap, or Material
options.description: Red itchy rash limited to the specific skin area that touched an irritant or allergen (poisons, detergents, jewelry).
options.warning: Wash affected skin thoroughly to remove lingering irritants.
first_aid_steps: Wash the affected skin gently with mild soap and cool water.
Apply over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream or calamine lotion.
Avoid scratching to prevent secondary skin infection.
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if rash spreads widely, blisters, or shows signs of infection (pus, warmth).

initial_question: What type of cough or throat issue are you experiencing?

options.label: Coughing Up Bright Red Blood or Blood-Tinged Mucus
options.description: Expelling blood when coughing, which can signal serious airway or lung vascular conditions.
options.warning: 🚨 CRITICAL WARNING: Coughing up blood requires immediate hospital emergency evaluation.
first_aid_steps: Call 112 or go to the nearest hospital emergency room immediately.
Sit upright leaning slightly forward to prevent blood aspiration.
Keep calm and avoid physical exertion.
Save coughing sample in a tissue if possible for medical inspection.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate 112 emergency care.

options.label: Severe Sore Throat with Painful Swallowing & White Spots on Tonsils
options.description: Intense throat inflammation, pain when swallowing food/water, swollen neck glands, and high fever.
options.subtype_name: Severe Sore Throat / Suspected Strep or Tonsillitis
options.warning: May require prescription antibiotics if bacterial infection is confirmed.
first_aid_steps: Gargle with warm salt water (1/2 tsp salt in 1 cup warm water) 3-4 times daily.
Sip warm teas with honey or suck on throat lozenges.
Take over-the-counter pain relievers for throat pain if tolerated.
Stay well hydrated with soft liquids.
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if swallowing liquids is impossible or fever exceeds 102°F (38.9°C).

options.label: Dry Tickly Cough with Mild Throat Irritation
options.description: Irritating dry cough without mucus, commonly associated with viral colds or dry air.
options.warning: Keep throat moist with warm fluids.
first_aid_steps: Drink warm fluids like lemon honey tea or warm water.
Use a room cool-mist humidifier.
Avoid smoke, dust, and cold dry air.
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if dry cough lasts longer than 3 weeks.

initial_question: What symptoms accompany your nausea or vomiting?

options.label: Vomiting Bright Red Blood or Dark 'Coffee-Ground' Material
options.description: Vomiting containing fresh red blood or dark brown/black digested blood flakes, indicating upper GI bleeding.
options.warning: 🚨 CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Vomiting blood or coffee-ground material requires immediate emergency care.
first_aid_steps: Call 112 or transport to emergency room immediately.
Keep person sitting upright or lying on their side (recovery position) to prevent choking/aspiration.
Do not give any food, water, or oral medications.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate 112 emergency response.

options.label: Sudden Repeated Vomiting & Diarrhea After Eating Questionable Food
options.description: Acute stomach upset, vomiting, watery stools, and abdominal cramps within hours of eating contaminated food.
options.warning: Prevent dehydration by taking small frequent sips of fluids.
first_aid_steps: Let the stomach rest for 1-2 hours after vomiting stops.
Sip small amounts (teaspoon at a time) of Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) or electrolyte water.
Gradually introduce bland foods like crackers, toast, or bananas.
Rest in a cool, quiet room.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a doctor if unable to keep any fluids down for 24 hours or if signs of severe dehydration appear.

options.label: Mild Nausea from Travel, Motion, or Morning Sickness (Female/Pregnancy Alert)
options.description: Queasiness related to movement, pregnancy, or temporary mild indigestion.
options.warning: Fresh air, ginger, and small bland meals help settle pregnancy or motion nausea.
first_aid_steps: Get fresh air and look at a fixed horizon point.
Sip ginger tea, ginger ale, or peppermint tea.
Eat small frequent dry snacks (like crackers) before getting out of bed for morning sickness.
Avoid heavy, greasy, or strong-smelling foods.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Consult a physician if hyperemesis gravidarum (severe pregnancy vomiting preventing fluid retention) develops.

initial_question: What kind of joint or back pain are you experiencing?

options.label: Severe Low Back Pain with Groin Numbness or Loss of Bowel/Bladder Control
options.description: Severe lower spine pain combined with loss of sensation in groin/buttocks ('saddle anesthesia') or sudden incontinence.
options.warning: 🚨 CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Cauda Equina syndrome is a surgical spinal emergency. Immediate care needed.
first_aid_steps: Call 112 or transport to nearest emergency trauma center immediately.
Keep the person lying flat and still. Avoid twisting or bending the spine.
Do not give any food or drink in case emergency spinal surgery is required.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate 112 emergency response.

options.label: Sudden Intensely Painful, Red, Hot, & Swollen Single Joint (e.g. Toe/Knee)
options.description: Acute onset of extreme joint tenderness, swelling, redness, and heat in a single joint, unable to bear weight.
options.subtype_name: Suspected Acute Gout Attack or Septic Arthritis
options.warning: Requires urgent medical evaluation to rule out joint infection (septic joint). (Note: Gout is significantly more common in adult males).
first_aid_steps: Rest and elevate the affected joint above heart level.
Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth to joint for 15-20 minutes.
Avoid putting weight on the joint.
Seek prompt medical evaluation.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Seek urgent medical clinic evaluation within 24 hours.

options.label: Dull Ache in Lower Back or Joint After Heavy Lifting or Activity
options.description: Muscular stiffness or ache following physical strain, exercise, or improper lifting posture.
options.warning: Rest the back and avoid re-injury.
first_aid_steps: Rest in a comfortable position (lying on side with a pillow between knees).
Apply ice pack for first 48 hours, then warm compresses to relax stiff muscles.
Perform gentle walking as tolerated to prevent stiffness.
options.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if back pain radiates down legs below knees or does not improve after 1 week.

initial_question: What kind of hand or arm pain are you experiencing?

options.label: Sudden Arm Pain with Chest Pressure, Shortness of Breath, or Sweating
options.description: Sudden onset of left or right arm pain accompanied by chest heaviness, breathlessness, cold sweat, or nausea.
options.warning: 🚨 CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Arm pain combined with chest pressure or breathlessness is a heart attack warning indicator.
first_aid_steps: Call 112 (or local emergency medical services) immediately.
Stop all physical activity immediately and sit down in a comfortable position.
Loosen tight clothing around neck and chest.
Do NOT attempt to drive yourself to the hospital.
Monitor breathing and alertness until paramedics arrive.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Immediate emergency room / 112 dispatch required.

options.label: Sudden Pain After Fall/Impact with Deformed Bone or Inability to Move
options.description: Severe localized pain after trauma, with visible bone deformity, intense swelling, or inability to move wrist/fingers.
options.subtype_name: Suspected Hand / Wrist Fracture or Dislocation
options.warning: Requires urgent orthopedic X-ray, splinting, and immobilization.
first_aid_steps: Immobilize the hand/arm using a pillow or sling.
Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth to reduce swelling.
Do NOT try to push protruding bone back in or force hand into position.
Transport safely to hospital emergency room or urgent care center.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Urgent hospital emergency evaluation required.

options.label: Numbness, Tingling, or Shooting 'Pins & Needles' in Thumb/Fingers
options.description: Nerve discomfort radiating down forearm into thumb, index, or middle finger, often worse at night or after typing.
options.warning: Avoid wrist flexing and repetitive hand strain.
first_aid_steps: Rest hand and keep wrist in a straight neutral position.
Avoid repetitive typing, heavy gripping, or vibrating tools.
Wear a supportive wrist splint, especially at night.
Apply cold compress for 15 minutes to reduce wrist joint swelling.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Schedule physician or neurologist evaluation if hand numbness or weakness persists.

options.label: Dull Ache, Stiffness, or Minor Swelling in Wrist/Fingers After Overuse
options.description: Muscular ache or tendon stiffness following sports, computer work, or repetitive lifting.
options.warning: Follow R.I.C.E protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation).
first_aid_steps: Rest the hand and take regular breaks from repetitive work.
Apply cold compress for 15-20 minutes 3 times daily.
Elevate hand on a pillow when resting to decrease fluid buildup.
Perform gentle finger and wrist range-of-motion stretches.
options.when_to_see_doctor: Consult doctor if pain persists over 1 week or prevents daily activities.

initial_question: What best describes your leg or foot pain?

options.label: Sudden severe pain after fall/injury
options.description: Possible fracture or ligament rupture

options.label: Twisted ankle / Sprain with swelling
options.description: Soft tissue or joint strain

options.label: Muscle cramp or mild ache
options.description: Fatigue, dehydration, or mild strain
